title: About me
goal: Introduce yourself — your name, where you're from, where you live and what languages you speak — and ask others the same.
intro:
In this unit you meet the Sindhi personal pronouns and learn to use **آهيان / آهي / آهيو** ('am / is / are') with all of them. You'll also learn the main question words, so you can ask *who, what, where* and *where from*.

Notice the Sindhi way of saying where you're from: **مان ڪراچيءَ جو آهيان** — literally 'I am *of* Karachi'.

grammar.title: Personal pronouns and 'to be'
grammar.body:
Sindhi pronouns have a **direct** form (used as the subject) and an **oblique** form (used before postpositions like جو 'of', کي 'to', ۾ 'in'):

مان / آئون (I) → مون moṃ
تون (you, intimate) → تو to
هو (he, that) / هوءَ (she) → هن hun
هي (this, he/she here) → هن hin
اسين (we) → اسان asāṃ
توهين / توهان (you, polite) → توهان tavhāṃ
هو (they) → هنن hunan

There is **no separate word for 'it'**: use هي (this) or هو / اهو (that). Third person distinguishes **near** (هي) from **far** (هو / هوءَ).

The verb آهي 'is' follows the subject: مان آهيان, تون آهين, هو/هوءَ آهي, اسين آهيون, توهان آهيو, هو آهن.

grammar.title: Question words and yes/no questions
grammar.body:
Question words go **where the answer would go** — usually just before the verb — not at the start as in English: 'Your name *what* is?'

ڇا chhā what · ڪير ker who · ڪٿي kithe where · ڪٿان kithāṃ from where · ڪڏهن kaɗahiṃ when · ڇو chho why · ڪيئن kīeṃ how · ڪهڙو kahiṛo which.

For a **yes/no question**, either just raise your voice at the end, or put **ڇا** at the very beginning (a bit more formal): ڇا توهان سنڌي آهيو؟ 'Are you Sindhi?'

To say where someone is from, Sindhi uses **جو** 'of': مان ڪراچيءَ جو آهيان 'I'm of Karachi'. جو agrees with the person: جو for a man, جي for a woman, جا for plural or polite توهان. Place names ending in -ī add ءَ before a postposition (ڪراچي → ڪراچيءَ).

dialogue.title: At a university event
dialogue.setting: Sarah, a visiting student, meets Marvi at a cultural evening at Sindh University, Jamshoro.

lines.speaker: Marvi
lines.native: السلام عليڪم! توهان جو نالو ڇا آهي؟
lines.roman: assalāmu ʿalaikum! tavhāṃ jo nālo chhā āhe?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: وعليڪم السلام. منهنجو نالو سارا آهي.
lines.roman: vaʿalaikum assalām. munhinjo nālo Sārā āhe.

lines.speaker: Marvi
lines.native: مان ماروي آهيان. توهان ڪٿان جا آهيو؟

lines.en: I'm Marvi. Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Sarah

lines.speaker: Marvi

lines.roman: vāh! chhā tavhāṃ sindhī ɠālhāyo thā?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: ٿوري ٿوري. مان سمجهان ٿي، پر آهستي.
lines.roman: thorī thorī. māṃ samujhāṃ thī, para āhistī.
lines.en: A little. I understand, but slowly.

lines.en: No problem! I also speak a little English.

lines.speaker: Marvi
lines.native: منهنجو ڳوٺ ٿر ۾ آهي، مٺيءَ ويجهو.

lines.en: My village is in Thar, near Mithi.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: توهان سان ملي ڏاڍي خوشي ٿي!
lines.roman: tavhāṃ sāṃ mile ɗāḍhī xushī thī!

culture: Sindh is Pakistan's southern province, stretching from the Arabian Sea and the Indus delta to the Thar desert in the east. Karachi, its capital, is Pakistan's largest city and very multilingual (Urdu dominates), while Hyderabad, Sukkur, Larkana, Nawabshah, Mirpurkhas and the countryside are strongly Sindhi-speaking. After Partition in 1947 many Hindu Sindhis migrated to India, where Sindhi is a scheduled language and is written both in the Arabic-based script and in Devanagari; Indian cities such as Ulhasnagar, Ahmedabad and Mumbai have large Sindhi communities. Asking ‘where is your village?’ is a natural opening question in Sindh — many city-dwellers keep strong ties to their ancestral ڳوٺ.

lessons.title: Who is who: I, we, he and she

tip.title: Pronouns and "is"
tip.body:
- **مان** (or **آئون**) I · **اسين** we · **هو** he / that / they · **هوءَ** she · **هي** this, he or she (here).
- 'Is' follows the person: مان **آهيان**, اسين **آهيون**, هو/هوءَ **آهي**, they **آهن**.
- There is no 'it': say هي 'this' or هو 'that'.

lessons.title: Your name and where you are from

tip.title: Question words go where the answer goes
tip.body:
- Sindhi doesn't move question words to the front: 'your name **what** is?' = توهان جو نالو **ڇا** آهي؟
- **ڪٿي** where · **ڪٿان** from where · **ڪير** who · **ڇا** what.
- 'From' a place is 'of' a place: مان ڪراچيءَ **جو** آهيان (man), **جي** (woman), **جا** (توهان, plural).

tip.title: I live in …: رهان ٿو / رهان ٿي
tip.body:
- 'I live in X' = **مان X ۾ رهان ٿو** (man) or **رهان ٿي** (woman).
- The ending follows the person: توهان **رهو ٿا**, هو/هوءَ **رهي ٿو / ٿي**, اسين **رهون ٿا**, they **رهن ٿا**.
- **هتي** 'here' and **اتي** 'there' need no ۾.

sentences.native: منهنجو ڳوٺ اتي آهي، شهر ويجهو.
sentences.roman: munhinjo ɠoṭhu ute āhe, shahara vejho.
sentences.en: My village is over there, near the city.

lessons.title: Do you speak Sindhi?

tip.title: Asking and answering about languages
tip.body:
- **ڇا** at the front makes a yes/no question: **ڇا** توهان سنڌي ڳالهايو ٿا؟
- The verb ending shows who: مان **ڳالهايان**, توهان **ڳالهايو**, هو/هوءَ **ڳالهائي**.
- Then **ٿو** for a man, **ٿي** for a woman, **ٿا** with توهان.
- 'Don't' = **نٿو / نٿي** before the verb: مان نٿو سمجهان.

new: مان سمجهان ٿو، پر ڳالهائي نٿو سگهان.

sentences.native: ها، مان انگريزي ۽ اردو ڳالهايان ٿو.
sentences.roman: hā, māṃ angrezī ai urdū ɠālhāyāṃ tho.
sentences.en: Yes, I speak English and Urdu. (man)

tip.title: More question words
tip.body:
- **ڪهڙو** 'which' agrees like an adjective: ڪهڙو شهر (m), ڪهڙي ٻولي (f).
- **ڪڏهن** 'when' and **ڇو** 'why' sit just before the verb.
- **به** 'too' comes after its word: مان **به** 'me too'.
- 'I don't know' = **مون کي خبر ناهي** (lit. to me there is no knowledge).

sentences.roman: tavhāṃ kahiṛe shahara meṃ raho thā?
sentences.en: Which city do you live in?
Why are you here? (to a friend)

sentences.native: معاف ڪجو، مون کي خبر ناهي.
sentences.roman: māf kajo, moṃ khe xabara nāhe.
